overall_reason: The page shows its own product instead of describing it: a fan of real theme renders, a draggable before/after comparison of one prompt with issue counts, real install commands and named builds; the editorial-serif look is the product's own subject matter, though a few stock beats (grid-line hero texture, FAQ, closing install band) remain.

findings.evidence: Faint orange graph-paper grid with vertical guide lines behind the h1 (sweep gradient hits on span.guides--l/--r); the same blueprint-grid hero texture is a common default on dev-tool pages. T-DELETION: removing it loses nothing, the fan of theme renders already carries the hero.
findings.before: Grid lines + orange guides behind the headline
findings.after: Plain paper behind the h1; let the theme fan be the only image
findings.why: One borrowed decoration on an otherwise specific first screen.

findings.where: section order (from dom-1440 text; tiles 03-07 did not render, see not_investigated)
findings.evidence: T-STOCK-ORDER: hero, comparison, 'It designs before it codes' four steps (Asks / Deals / Lays out / Checks), theme grid, 'Same theme, different pages', 'Questions' FAQ, 'Made with Hallmark' wheel, dark install footer band. Stock beats present: 4-step how-it-works, FAQ, CTA/install band, footer (4, below the 5 threshold). The comparison and the wheel are not stock.
findings.before: Four-step 'how it works' + FAQ + install band
findings.after: Fold the four steps into the comparison (show each step on the farm-records example) so the page keeps one argument
findings.why: The middle of the page falls back to the standard explainer rhythm after a distinctive opening.

findings.evidence: 'Without 26 issues' vs 'With Hallmark 0 issues', and the note 'The issue counts come from Hallmark's linter.' The proof is graded by the product's own checker.
findings.after: Keep the counts but name what the 26 are on hover, or add an independent measure [DATA NEEDED: third-party or human review result]
findings.why: Honest that it is self-measured, which is good, but a 26-to-0 score from your own tool reads as a stat band without a source.

findings.evidence: T-FRESH-READER: the three lines that could fit another site are 'The design skill that ends AI slop.' (category claim any rival skill would make, fails T-RIVAL-NAME), 'One prompt, two pages', 'Questions'. The h1 is the only one in the hero.
findings.before: "The design skill that ends AI slop."
findings.after: A head only this product can say, e.g. naming the mechanism ('Fifty themes, real photographs, and a linter that checks its own page')
findings.why: The headline is the least specific line on a specific page.

strengths: The hero shows the output: a fanned deal of real theme pages (Fieldbook, Tilly, Relay, Driftsong, Field Office) with a 'Deal again' control; the visual is the product.
Before/after comparison on one prompt with tabs (Farm records, Bank reconciliation, Webhook API) and a drag divider: falsifiable, picturable, only-this-business.
Install command in the first screen and a closing table of real commands ('/hallmark redesign <path>', '~/.claude/skills/hallmark').
Footer credits named people ('Created by Hassan and Youssef') and a real star count.
not_investigated: Tiles 1440-03 to 07 and 375-04 onward are blank: scroll-reveal sections never painted in the full-page capture (sweep ROB-001: 66% hidden after load). Focus crops (e.g. focus/31-on.png 'Show all 50 themes') show the content renders when scrolled to, so the empty bands are a capture limit and were not judged as design.
